findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and why it matters, in plain words. On that alone, a newcomer could describe the project.
findings.source: header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: There is a link to the next step at the top. The Next steps section gives a clone command, prerequisites, `./setup.sh` and a first `athena ask` command, so a newcomer knows what to do next.
findings.source: header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the Next steps section

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but nearly all of the page explains another project's internals: exit codes, lock contention and pending-close replays. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to scroll past a long firstmate state machine that has little to do with their question.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title>; sections States, Counters, Transitions t1–t12

findings.text: The page promises that Athena traces work to models, cost and a verdict, but this sample of Athena's output never shows which models made the study, what it cost, or what the checker decided. The main selling point is stated but never demonstrated.
findings.source: lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost"

findings.text: The page says Athena is written in Rust, but the prerequisites do not mention a Rust toolchain or say whether setup.sh installs one. They also say nothing about supported operating systems or the model access or cost the reader needs. A newcomer may hit surprises during install.
findings.source: Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm"

findings.text: The page never explains who the "owner" is or what these proposals are. To a newcomer this link reads as internal and confusing.
findings.source: header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision"

findings.text: These passages use Athena's internal vocabulary (job, recorded boundary, the studies/ folder) without saying what it means or which repository holds the folder.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate"; About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/"

findings.text: Some terms appear before they are explained or are never explained: PR is defined only in the end-of-page Glossary, and the Glossary says captain call is undefined. This adds friction for a reader who doesn't already know the field.
findings.source: "Words used first": "green — A PR that is not red"; "One piece of work" step 7: "still an open captain call"
